title: Is the missing action inverse_transform the mechanism behind invalid LeWM closed-loop control?
design: single-variable ablation: process['action'] transform (identity vs dataset-estimated StandardScaler)

predecessor.note: 0001L observed failure but did not verify its mechanism; 0002 isolates the mechanism.

action_scaler_source.caveat: partial Parquet shard, NOT the official full training dataset; scaler is an approximation

K2_scaler_condition_within_play_area.detail: 2/8 episodes still out of play; block displacement median remains 0.0

mechanism_evidence.policy_postprocess: policy.py calls process['action'].inverse_transform before env step
mechanism_evidence.scale_mismatch: CEM sampling std 1.0 vs expert action std ~0.19 (5.3x)

confounder_not_resolved.issue: tasks are randomly sampled, not dataset-defined
confounder_not_resolved.evidence: start-to-goal distance up to 360.9 with strict pose alignment (pos_diff<20, angle_diff<pi/9)
confounder_not_resolved.why_it_matters: 0/8 success must NOT be read as model capability; official protocol uses same-episode states 25 steps apart, which are reachable by construction

post_hoc_correction.issue: a 2-episode smoke suggested full repair (out-of-play 0/2, block displacement mean 112.28)
post_hoc_correction.correction: at 8 episodes the block-displacement MEDIAN is 0.0; the smoke number was inflated by a single 208.36 outlier
post_hoc_correction.recurrence: this repeats the zero-inflated heavy-tail mistake already recorded in project MEMORY.md

allowed_claim: Under fixed tasks and planner configuration, adding an action inverse_transform estimated from public data reduces LeWM agent excursions out of the play area from 8/8 to 2/8 and produces real block interaction in 3/8 episodes; the missing transform is part of the KW-LEWM-0001L failure mechanism.
forbidden_claims: LeWM compared against JEPA-WM or any competitor
the approximate scaler equals the official full-dataset scaler
